title: Tigers GM Jeff Greenberg removes name from consideration for Red Wings job
content:
DETROIT — Detroit Tigers general manager Jeff Greenberg has removed his name from consideration for the Detroit Red Wings’ vacant head of hockey operations position, Greenberg communicated Monday through a Tigers spokesperson.

Greenberg has informed the Red Wings of the decision and, per the spokesperson, said he has “tremendous respect and admiration for the organization and was honored to be considered for the opportunity, but he is committed to the Tigers and what this group is building.”

Greenberg joined the Tigers in September 2023, when president of baseball operations Scott Harris hired him away from the NHL’s Chicago Blackhawks, where Greenberg served as associate general manager starting in April 2022.

Harris and Greenberg previously worked together in the Chicago Cubs front office under Theo Epstein, and Greenberg rose to Cubs assistant general manager before his foray into hockey. The Tigers have made playoff appearances in each of the past two seasons but are amid a disappointing year, entering Monday with a 65-78 record.

The Red Wings — who share ownership with the Tigers under the Ilitch Sports + Entertainment umbrella — remain in a lengthy search for their new head of hockey operations. The team announced on July 15 that former general manager Steve Yzerman would transition to senior adviser for CEO Chris Ilitch. The Red Wings open training camp Sept. 17 and start their season Oct. 2 against the New York Rangers.
